messages:
support-ops: Customer C escalated high latency for /v1/generate from EU users at ~09:12 UTC. p95 jumped from ~80ms -> ~480ms, p99 ~1.2s. No increase in 5xx. Ticket: https://support.redwood/c/1145 :rotating_light:

maria: copying the traces we have from their synthetic probes and our edge metrics. They see TLS handshake dominated time in eu-west POPs.
\maria: probe summary: client -> anycast -> eu-west-pop -> origin. traceroute shows an extra hop shift in last 2 mins.
\maria: traceroute snippet:
```
traceroute to api.redwood.example (52.17.34.21), 30 hops max
 1  10.0.0.1  1.0 ms
 2  203.0.113.5  4.2 ms
 3  198.51.100.7  6.9 ms
 4  198.51.100.12  75.4 ms  <-- unexpected cross-az hop
 5  52.17.34.21  78.2 ms
```

jon: weird, that 75ms jump looks like a cross-region hairpin or a bad peering path. Any DNS changes?

maria: DNS TTL for our GSLB was 30s (unchanged). No config pushes from infra in the last 24h.

lee: grabbed tcpdump at eu-west-edge-3 during the spike, TLS handshake timings:
```
ClientHello -> ServerHello time ~220ms (handshake delays)
Full handshake -> application data ~240ms
No retransmits obvious in 5-tuple window we captured
```

network-eng: seeing BGP path change in provider X around 09:08 UTC to a suboptimal peer. This matches the timing. Provider shows short flap and withdrawal.

maria: @network-eng can you post the BGP/peering diff? If it's a peering change we might have had traffic shift to a POP with heavier cross-az transit.

network-eng: pasted AS path diff (sanitized):
```
before: ... -> AS65010 -> AS65020 -> eu-west-pop
after:  ... -> AS65010 -> AS65432 -> AS65020 -> eu-west-pop  (added hop via transit)
```

jon: that additional hop explains TLS handshake addl RTT. For long-tail (p99) it amplifies queuing. Two immediate mitigations: 1) pin critical customers to eu-west-pop-1 (nearest) using routing override 2) increase warm pool + pre-warmed connections in the fallback zone so handshakes happen to warmed endpoints.

support-ops: Customer asked for a quick mitigation — can we do #1 now? They can't accept 400ms p95.

lee: I can apply a temporary routing policy to pin their requests to eu-west-pop-1 via a customer-level tag. Will take ~3-5 min to propagate, need ack to proceed.

maria: do it. Also flip their routing policy TTL to 300s so it sticks until we finish RCA. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: routing-policy: apply customer_tag=cust-c -> target_pop=eu-west-pop-1 -> status=queued
deploy-bot: routing-policy: apply customer_tag=cust-c -> target_pop=eu-west-pop-1 -> status=applied (propagated to edge in ~45s)

jon: after the pin, monitor p95/p99 and TLS handshake times. If we drop back to baseline, we'll call that an emergency mitigation.

maria: post-pin metrics: p95 down to ~95ms within 90s, p99 to ~180ms. Customer confirmed perceived latency improved. :white_check_mark:

network-eng: provider X confirmed they had an internal failover that routed some prefixes through a partner AS momentarily. They reverted the change at 09:22. We'll keep monitoring BGP RIB churn for next 24h.

lee: recommend the following follow-ups: 1) set longer GSLB health probing (to avoid rapid anycast shifts) 2) add provider X to our peering watchlist with alerts on AS path changes for critical prefixes 3) add an automated customer-pin option for high-severity SLAs.

jon: agree. Also, product should consider exposing a 'preferred-region' per-customer for premium plans (low risk mitigation).

support-ops: Customer C accepted the temporary pin and asked for RCA. I'll open a postmortem and link steps + timeline.

maria: I'll collect logs, pcap slices, and edge routing diffs and drop into the postmortem. Note for RCA: look at time correlation between probe DNS resolution, anycast handoff and BGP flaps.

network-eng: leaving provider X contact looped in. If we keep seeing intermittent AS path detours we should throttle failover sensitivity in our GSLB.

jon: cool — we'll keep the routing pin for 6 hours while we finish the RCA. After that, revert unless we have a config change.

support-ops: closing the immediate escalation with customer. Will update ticket with mitigation and ETA for RCA (EOD). Thanks all.

maria: follow-up action items assigned in postmortem doc. Good catch on the handshake timings everyone.

lee: TL;DR: transient provider peering detour caused extra hop -> TLS handshake inflation -> p95/p99 spike. Mitigated by customer-level pop pin + warm-pool increases.

jon: moving to postmortem/ops-track. Marking thread resolved unless new alerts surface. :lock:
